questions.prompt: About how many tokens is a 600-word English text, using the vendors' rule of thumb?

options.explanation: Right. 1 token is about 0.75 English words, so 600 ÷ 0.75 = 800.
A token is not a word. The rule is about 0.75 words per token.
That divides by 4, which is the characters-per-token rule, not the words rule.

questions.prompt: You switch your app to a newer model. What happens to your measured token counts?

options.text: They may change, because the new model can use a different tokenizer. Recount.
options.explanation: Right. The Claude docs give a newer tokenizer that produces about 30% more tokens for the same text.

options.text: They stay the same. Tokens depend only on the text, not on the model that reads it.
options.explanation: Tokens depend on the text and on the model's tokenizer.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT counted as input tokens?

options.text: The tokens in the model's reply.
options.explanation: Right. The reply is output. Input and output are counted and priced separately.

options.text: The tool definitions in the request.
options.explanation: Tool names, descriptions and schemas are sent with the request, so they are input.

options.text: The system prompt in the request.
options.explanation: The system prompt is part of the request, so it is input.

options.text: Images in the user message, resized.
options.explanation: Images are converted to tokens and count as input.
